title: Cross-tenant quota pooling, spillover rules, and overage billing PRD
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Overview: Large enterprise customers frequently manage multiple Redwood accounts (orgs, teams, or product lines) and want flexible quota economics across them. This PRD proposes a feature to allow customers to create a cross-tenant quota pool (shared token/embedding quota) with configurable spillover rules and automated pro-rata billing/chargeback for overages.

Goals:
- Enable customers to group multiple Redwood accounts under a single shared quota pool to reduce unused entitlements and simplify operations.
- Define deterministic spillover behavior when a single account exceeds its allocation (preferred peers, prioritization, hard caps).
- Ensure clear billing semantics: how usage is billed (owner-charged, pro-rata from member accounts, or centralized invoice), rollover interactions, and overage calculations.
- Provide admin UI/Console controls and API for pool creation, membership, priority configuration, and audit logs.

Out of Scope:
- Cross-cloud credit transfers between different cloud providers (separate follow-up).
- Automated migration of existing quotas into pools without admin confirmation.

Success metrics:
- Pilot with 3 enterprise customers representing >$50k monthly usage within quarter after GA.
- Pool-backed accounts show 15% lower wasted quota vs. baseline after 30 days.
- Fewer billing support tickets for cross-account usage disputes (target <10 tickets in first month).
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create a named quota pool with an owner account and add/remove up to 50 member accounts via Console and API.
Pool configuration options include: fixed allocation per member, weighted shares (integer weights), and 'unbounded' share with hard global cap.
Spillover rules support three modes: disabled (no spillover), prioritized (specify ordered fallback list), and open (first-available consumption).

When a member account consumes beyond its personal allocation, system applies spillover rules and records a detailed log entry per request showing source allocation, pool consumption, and remaining quota.

Billing semantics implemented: (a) centralized-billing mode: pool owner billed for all usage; (b) pro-rata mode: overage split by weights at invoice period boundary; (c) pass-through mode: using account of origin for all charges including overage. Mode is selectable per pool.
Usage reporting in Console shows per-account and per-pool breakdowns with token counts, embedding units, and estimated dollar cost, and supports CSV export for audit.
API surfaces to retrieve pool membership, current balances, historical usage windows, and to simulate overage charges for a hypothetical month.
All pool actions (create, update, delete, membership changes) are captured in audit logs with admin identity and timestamp; logs integrate with existing KMS/HSM-backed audit pipeline.

Billing acceptance checks: invoices reflect pool mode accurately (centralized invoice lines or per-account adjustments), and pro-rata calculations reconcile against raw usage within <1% rounding error.
SLO: pool creation/update API overall latency <500ms p95 and reporting queries return within 1s p95 for 30-day windows for pools with <=50 members.
Automated tests and e2e scenarios cover at least: single-member overflow, prioritized spillover chain, weighted-pro-rata billing split, and pool deletion with residual usage handling.
billing_acceptance_criteria: Invoice line-items must include pool identifier, billing mode, and explicit per-account charge details when pro-rata or pass-through mode is used.

Pro-rata overage calculation algorithm documented and deterministic: use total overage units * member_weight / sum(member_weights), round to nearest cent with always-sum-equals-total adjustment applied to highest-weight member.
Edge-case handling: when a member account is closed mid-invoice-period, remaining owed charges are allocated proportionally among remaining active members for that period.
Billing events matched to raw usage logs with trace IDs to support disputability; reconciliation script produces a diff report with tolerances and flags >1% variance.
Admin Console shows a projected month-end invoice for the pool and a 'simulate charges' button to preview pro-rata splits for anticipated spikes.
Billing alerts triggered when projected overage > 20% of pool allocation or when any single member is consuming >70% of pool usage for 24h.

Invoices for pools in centralized-billing mode are issued to pool owner account; for pass-through mode invoices remain per-origin account; for pro-rata both aggregated and per-account attachments are available.
notes: Design tradeoffs discussed 2026-02-27: prefer explicit pool owner (simpler legal/billing ownership) over fully decentralized pools; may revisit multi-owner in future.
Privacy: pool members cannot view other members' raw invoices unless granted 'billing-view' RBAC permission; Console UI will mask PII in shared reports by default.
Integration: requires small Billing service change to support 'pool_id' metadata on invoice lines and invoice preview endpoint; downstream accounting team sign-off needed.
Alternative considered: 'soft pooling' where unused quota is borrowed temporarily but returned first; rejected because it complicated billing reconciliation and dispute handling.
Prototype discussions with two pilot customers scheduled week of 2026-03-15; early feedback requested on naming (pool vs. umbrella vs. shared bucket) and UI terminology.
